learning_outcomes.text: Know the different types of matrices and their properties. Perform operations with matrices fluently.
Know and calculate the fundamental subspaces of a matrix.
Use matrix techniques to represent and solve a system of linear equations by previously checking its nature.
Know the concepts of vector space and subspace, linear dependence and independence, basis, and dimension.
Be able to calculate and know the change of basis matrices, as well as their properties.
Be able to competently handle vector subspaces, and to correctly determine and operate with their intersection and sum.
Be able to recognize linear transformations and determine their matrix representation.
Know the concepts of image and kernel of a linear transformation and be able to use them to classify them.
Be able to determine the matrices associated with a linear transformation with respect to different bases.
Understand and be able to use the metric concepts of scalar product, norm, orthogonality, and orthogonal projection.
Calculate an orthonormal basis from any basis.
Be able to calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors, as well as eigenspaces of an endomorphism.
Know and be able to apply criteria to identify diagonalizable matrices.
Be able to apply the diagonalization process to the calculation of powers of diagonalizable matrices.
Apply spectral techniques to solve engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Matrices and systems of linear equations

assessment_methods.method: Active participation in tutorials, attendance at programmed workshops, and student involvement (T)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, students can choose continuous or final evaluation. For continuous evaluation, the final grade is 0.75*E + 0.20*P + 0.05*T. For final evaluation, the final grade is 0.80*E + 0.20*P, and students must notify the faculty 15 days in advance. In both modalities, a minimum of 4.0 out of 10 points in the final development exam (E) and a final grade of 5.0 or higher are required to pass. In extraordinary calls, the final grade is 0.80*E + 0.20*P, with the same minimum requirements; students can choose to take the practical exam or keep the score from the ordinary call.
